items.headline: Nvidia reports fiscal Q3 revenue of $115.8B against about $108.8B expected, and guides Q4 to roughly $130B
items.why: Data center revenue of $107.6B (up 110% year over year) and a raised full-year growth outlook answer the question the market has been asking, whether AI infrastructure spending is still accelerating; the stock rose about 4% after hours.

sources.title: Nvidia earnings: live updates and commentary, November 2026

items.headline: Nvidia's chief executive leaves the company; the stock is down nearly 27% in November and the selloff spread to chipmakers and data center operators
items.why: Leadership risk landed on the single most important company in the AI build-out, so the earnings beat has to repair a confidence problem as well as a growth question; an interim chief executive is in place while a successor is sought.

sources.title: US inflation keeps pressure on the Fed as Nvidia's selloff spreads

items.headline: Anthropic launches its IPO roadshow: 825M Class A shares at an expected $70 to $78, to list on Nasdaq under ANT
items.why: The largest AI-lab listing to date arrives in the middle of an AI-stock drawdown, so its pricing and first-day trading will be read as a direct test of public-market appetite for AI valuations.

sources.title: Anthropic launches roadshow for proposed initial public offering

items.headline: US spot bitcoin ETFs lose $1.07B for a second straight week above $1B; bitcoin dips below $69,000, lowest since August 20
items.why: Seven straight days of ETF outflows (about $1.91B) removed the main source of marginal demand, and the funds are now down about $1.98B for 2026; ether ETFs lost $398.9M, their seventh negative week.

items.headline: Crypto sold off with the rates repricing: bitcoin fell about 2.5% to near $73,000 and ether about 5% on the hot CPI print, then slid to roughly $65,650 by Saturday
items.why: Crypto traded as a rate-sensitive risk asset this week, so a hawkish Fed path is the variable to watch rather than anything crypto-specific.

items.headline: October CPI beats: headline +0.4% month on month versus 0.3% expected, core +0.3% for a third straight month
items.why: Core running at 0.3% a month keeps a December rate hike as the base case, with one Fed governor floating a 50 basis point move if it persists, and the 2-year Treasury yield jumped about 20 bps to 4.76% on the print.

items.headline: Gulf conflict stays hot: tankers hit in the Strait of Hormuz, repeated Iranian attacks on a US base in Bahrain, and a third US carrier arrives, while the US rejects Iran's core ceasefire conditions
items.why: Hormuz is still closed to normal traffic and no deal is in sight, so the oil risk premium and the inflation path both stay hostage to events; a 10-nation regional bloc backing Iran's reopening plan has not moved Washington.

items.headline: Brent holds near $95 (US crude about $88) on Hormuz disruption, far above the roughly $72 level before the war began
items.why: Brent fell 16% the week to November 6 on talks optimism and has since stalled; with Gulf supply still contested, oil is trading headlines rather than inventories, and diesel just dipped below $6 a gallon for the first time since September.

items.headline: Gold gives back its prior-week rally, falling to about $3,885 and back near its one-year low after the hot CPI; the gold-silver ratio rises above 80
items.why: Higher real yields and a stronger dollar are outweighing the war premium, and the widening ratio shows silver is the weaker leg of the precious-metals complex.

items.headline: Gold sits just above its $3,869.85 one-year low, under the $4,197 to $4,202 average cluster; Brent has the 200-day average near $93.24 as its next level
items.why: Gold needs to reclaim the 50- and 100-day averages to confirm any recovery, while a hold above the 200-day on Brent keeps the post-drop range intact; a break of either is the structural signal.
